newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark faces tough hurdle above 1.6820.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark faces tough hurdle above 1.6820.

text.p: The dollar benefitted from mark weakness against the yen and Swiss franc crosses to rise to a new 33-month high at 1.6810 marks on Tuesday, technical analysts said.

However, the U.S. unit quickly fell and stabilized just above its 1.6755 mark support, last Friday's 32-month high, and faces tough resistance from 1.6820 to 1.6850 marks. Dealers cited 1.6280 as the next dollar/mark upside target.

"We were advising to take profits at the 1.6820/50 area, so that zone for us becomes the next band we would need to breach to become bullish dollars," said Darren Spain, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston Corp.
Layers of support now lie at 1.6755, 1.6650 and 1.66 marks.
Against the yen, the mark slipped past its 73.50 post-G7 summit low to hit a nadir of 73.26.
Analysts said mark/yen's downside near-term target is 72.50, just above the January lows. Minor support was cited at 73 the figure.
Mark/yen resistance lies at 73.50 and then the overnight support of 73.80, but Spain said a return to those levels in the short-run was "not on the cards".
Meanwhile, dollar/yen was confined within Monday's ranges, bolstered by the slide in mark/yen. A holiday Tuesday in Tokyo reduced trade activity in the pair, dealers said.

Dealers saw any rise in the dollar capped at 123/40 yen and support at 122.30 yen. "To have upside strength, dollar/yen has got to hold above 121.90. If it doesn't, we will go into one of those big, whipping trade ranges here," said John Tirone, technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc.

Sterling captured a new 52-month peak at 2.7532 marks and reached a high of $1.6452. A U.S. close above $1.6410/20 would be the highest closing rate since sterling's sharp fall beginning January 22, Tirone said.
By late trade, the British pound had dipped below $1.64 to trade around $1.6370.
"The only way you are going to do any damage is if you get below $1.6280 -- that's a big area," Tirone said.
